OmniPad PS5
Universal Controller Engine & Web Control Center for PlayStation 5 (FW 7.00 – 13.60)

### Legal Disclaimer & Fair Use Notice
This is an independent open-source research project developed strictly for educational, accessibility, and hardware interoperability purposes (allowing third-party controllers and adaptive peripherals to function on the console).

"Honestly? This whole project started because I was just a guy who wanted his Machenike G5 Pro Max SE controller working on his PS5."

I wanted to play 3-player and 4-player local games on my jailbroken PS5 (running FW 13.60 with kstuff and shadowmountplus). However, existing community tools either lacked 2.4GHz USB dongle hotplug support or broke on FW 13.60's user profile assignment screen (0x803B0006).

release.title: OmniPad PS5 v1.0.4 - Hotfix 1 (Build 19)
release.notes:
OmniPad PS5 v1.0.4 - Hotfix 1 (Build 19)

Hotfix release resolving profile selection stall, wired USB connection drops, and clarifying connectivity roadmap.

Highlights & Bug Fixes

• Fixed Wired USB Stalls: Restricted Xbox 360 keepalive packets strictly to genuine Microsoft hardware, eliminating USB-C pipeline stalls on ShanWan / Machenike G5 Pro Max SE and third-party controllers.
• Clean Profile Picker (No Ghost "Connected" State): Completely resolved an issue where profiles would appear as already connected after logging out in-game; now smoothly triggers the clean native PS5 profile picker.
• Dynamic Handle Binding: Added dynamic scePadGetHandle synchronization inside the main polling loop. As soon as you select your profile on the PS5 screen, your controller immediately takes over gameplay.
• Extended 2.4G Standby Timeout: Increased idle timeout for 2.4GHz dongles from 5 seconds to 60 seconds (1 minute), avoiding abrupt disconnections.
• Safe Unbind Sequence: Controller release now decouples MBus before destroying the virtual pad, avoiding kernel error 0x809B00FF.
• Documentation Transparency: Clarified that direct internal Bluetooth is in active development for v1.1.0 to ensure full hardware safety, focusing v1.0.4 on 250Hz USB & 2.4GHz dongles.

Assets
• OmniPad-PS5-1.0.4.elf — Ready-to-run payload for PS5 (FW 7.00 - 13.60)

apps.name: DriftCheck
apps.author: felipemelchior
apps.description: Controller tester for jailbroken PS5
apps.about:
DriftCheck is a native PS5 homebrew app that shows everything your DualSense reports and
measures how healthy its analog sticks are. Run the rest test, let go of the sticks for three
seconds, and it tells you whether they drift and which deadzone would hide it.

(tools/preview.sh): the right stick rests off-centre and falls short of the edge.

A healthy stick rests within a few percent of the centre. DriftCheck calls 5 % and above
slight drift and 10 % and above drift. These thresholds are a starting point, not a
measured standard; the number itself is what to compare between controllers or before and after
a repair. The suggested deadzone is the resting distance rounded up plus two points. Set it in
the games that let you.

apps.name: PS5 PUP Decrypt Tool
apps.author: deepkicks
apps.description: A Python CLI tool that parses, analyzes, and decrypts PS5 PUP/BLS files on PC — no console required. Features BLS extraction, Layer 3 firmware decryption, PBKDF2/KMB key derivation, and entropy-based key testing. One key away from full PUP decryption for all firmware versions.
apps.about:
PC-based Python tool for parsing and decrypting PS5 PUP (PlayStation Update Package) files. No console needed.

The tool handles 3 of 4 crypto layers. Layer 1 (PUP container encryption) is the one missing piece — see RESEARCH_POST.md for the full technical write-up and what's needed.

Requires Python 3.10+, pycryptodome, and capstone (for automated handler disassembly).

If you have a jailbroken PS5 on FW 13.60 or below, ps5_key_extract.c implements a chained extraction strategy:

The chain: Approach 2 → automated RE → Approach 5
1. Dump the pup_update0 ioctl/open/close handler code (only needs kernel R/W)
2. Run analyze_dump.py on PC — it auto-disassembles the handlers and finds the key source
3. Re-run the payload with the -a command it gives you

release.title: PS5_Key_ExtractV4-Read-Only
release.notes:
• Goal: Extract the PUP container decryption key from a jailbroken PS5. This is the one missing key needed to decrypt PS5 firmware update files (PUP files) on PC.

• Target: The AMD CCP v5 (Cryptographic Co-Processor) and Sony’s EncryptService kernel driver (/dev/pup_update0). The PS5 uses this hardware+driver combo to decrypt firmware — the key lives in the CCP’s private key slots, which the CPU normally can’t read.

• Attack surface (default scan, no flags):

• CCP MMIO registers
• — reads the hardware’s public/private slot masks to see which key slots exist and which are CPU-accessible
Kernel cdevsw — finds Sony’s PUP decrypt driver in kernel memory, dumps the ioctl handler code (the function that actually calls the CCP to decrypt)
• CCP command queue
• — triggers a decrypt operation, then reads the raw CCP command descriptors the driver submitted. These reveal the exact AES mode, key size, and which slot number holds the key
Kernel symbol table — resolves sceSblServiceCrypt, sceSblSsDecryptPupHeader, etc. to get their addresses and dump their code.

Attack surface (with flags):

• -p — submits a CCP PASSTHROUGH command to copy a private key slot’s contents to readable memory. This is the extraction step — it bypasses the CPU read mask by having the CCP itself do the copy
• -d — feeds a real encrypted PUP header to the decrypt ioctl and captures the output (decryption oracle)

• What it doesn’t touch:
• No writes to flash, NVS, syscon, or kernel memory. The default scan…

release.title: ps5debug-NG v1.3.2
release.notes:
If you use ps5debug-NG, please star ⭐ the repo. It's free of charge and only takes a moment. :)

v1.3.0 was the big feature release. v1.3.2 is the correctness and reliability release that follows it: writes now prove they landed, three separate session-killing bugs are fixed, a scan comparator that silently returned wrong results is repaired, and firmware support extends through FW 13.60.

There was no separate v1.3.1 download, so this release also contains everything from v1.3.1 (Turbo Scan cancel).

Read this first: writes are now verified, and that changes what you see

Process writes used to report success as soon as the write was handed off. They are now read back and compared before success is reported, so a write that silently did nothing now correctly reports a failure.

If you are a client developer: a write that previously appeared to succeed may now return CMD_ERROR. That is the bug surfacing, not a new bug. Servers advertise capability level 1.1 so clients can detect the behaviour.

• CMD_PROC_WRITE returns terminal CMD_ERROR on write or verification failure.
• Write-multi returns typed per-entry status codes (invalid / DMAP / verify / mdbg) so you can tell exactly which entries failed and why, instead of losing the detail in one aggregate result.
• A proven DMAP mismatch no longer quietly falls through to the mdbg path.
• Caveat: a transfer whose start address ends in 0xFF backs up one byte to keep the write aligned. That adjacent-byte read-modify-write is not…

apps.name: PS5 BackPork
apps.author: BestPig
apps.description: Lets you sideload system libraries into PS5 games
apps.about:
A background payload for PlayStation 5 that automatically allows system library sideloading.

Backpork monitors game launches on the PS5. When a game (PPSA/CUSA title) is launched, it automatically mounts a fakelib folder from the game's app directory over the game's library path using unionfs. This allows for library replacement/injection without modifying originals files.

1. Game Launch Detection: When a game is launched, it retrieves the app info to get the title ID (PPSA/CUSA format)
2. Sandbox Discovery: Locates the game's sandbox directory at /mnt/sandbox/_XXX/
3. Fakelib Check: Checks if a fakelib folder exists in the game's app0 directory
4. Union Mount: If fakelibs exist, mounts them over the game's common/lib directory using unionfs
5. Cleanup: When the game exits, unmounts the fakelibs and cleans up the sandbox directory

Open the Settings tab in the web UI to edit /data/garlic/cloud.json.
You can also create the file manually:

The Browse tab exposes Cloud Backup actions for a selected save and for all saves under a title. Backups are encrypted/restorable ZIP archives. PS5 archives contain the raw save image; PS4 archives include the sdimg_... image and its .bin key companion when present.

What is new in 0.4.0

The graphics processor now draws the screen. Scaling the emulated picture
to 1920x1080 and storing it in the console's tiled display format is done by a
compute shader written in AMD GCN assembly, submitted through command packets
built by hand, because the console exposes its command processor and no
graphics API above it. Its output was checked against the processor routine it
replaced across the entire framebuffer and is byte-identical — zero of
4194304 words differ. It costs about 55 microseconds a frame where the
processor spent several milliseconds.

Half the emulated frames are no longer thrown away. A turn of the shell
draws once, but the loop running the emulator was running it twice, and the
first frame was overwritten before anyone saw it: six hundred frames emulated
for every three hundred shown. Measured on the same stretch of Sonic Adventure

of 17.5…

release.notes:

Fixed: USB drives listed other systems' games and held the start-up on a black screen

Seedee5 searched any roms folder on a USB or extended drive, even with the NAS turned off. Other systems' CHD, CUE and ISO files were listed as CD-i games, and on a big mechanical drive the search could keep the start-up on a black screen for half an hour.

• No more waiting: the drives are searched in the background. The wheel opens straight away, and their games join it when found; the top line shows the search.
• A safety limit: a search that meets more than 20,000 files stops and tells you to pick the folder.

Updating

Copy the PPSA99142 folder from Seedee5-1.24.zip over the old one in /data/homebrew/ over FTP, or update with ProsperoStore (your settings, NAS settings, saved games and BIOS come back by themselves).

PSP5 now follows the console's language, reads games and texture packs from USB drives, and lets you remap the PSP's buttons.

Interface language

Choose a language under Settings → System → Language and the home screen follows it, not just the emulator. 45 languages are available, including Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Lao. The font atlases were rebuilt to carry them, growing from 113 glyphs to 3,055 per face. Right-to-left languages are laid out right-to-left.

Where PPSSPP already translates a term, PSP5 uses its translation. The remainder — favourites, the A–Z view, the cheat panel, the save-state slots, the button names and the description under every settings row — are PSP5's own, shipped as 78 strings in 44 languages under assets/lang/psp5/.

These 78 strings are machine-translated and unreviewed in most languages. Corrections are a one-line edit in assets/lang/psp5/.ini: the files are plain English = translation, and a missing line falls back to English.

Games and texture packs on USB drives

PSP5 now reads drives using the same layout as its own memory stick:

All eight USB ports (/mnt/usb0 … /mnt/usb7) and both extended drives (/mnt/ext0, /mnt/ext1) are scanned. A texture pack on a drive takes precedence over one on the memory stick.

This requires folder listing to be unlocked. A PS5 app can open a file by its full path but cannot list a folder, and finding games requires listing. PSP5 requests the unlock at every start,…

release.title: GBAXY v2.3.0 by YAHBALLON
release.notes:
GBAXY v2.3.0 by YAHBALLON

(AI-assisted) Feature and stability release for PS5 Game Boy Advance homebrew (PPSA99209).

Improvements

• 7z ROMs (Issue #2): load single-GBA LZMA/LZMA2 archives from local storage, USB or NFS, with memory bounds and archive validation; existing .gba and .zip support remains.
• Smarter cover search: the Libretro GBA artwork index supports scene-dump prefixes (e.g. 1636 -), No-Intro/GoodTools region labels, Pokemon aliases, and conservative fuzzy name matching that rejects ambiguous sequels.
• Local ROM-folder cover override: My Game.gba, My Game.zip or My Game.7z uses My Game.png, My Game.jpg or My Game.jpeg in the same folder. Image filenames are matched case-insensitively; PNG takes priority. Local covers override manual covers, cached thumbnails and automatic download. Exact basename matching remains required (the temporary double-dot filename workaround has been removed).
• Triangle: Retry cover updates the selected artwork, checks the same ROM folder first (also when offline), and can discover an image uploaded while GBAXY is already open.
• Settings and stability: avoid dangling settings-row references on first save and synchronize the GPU when returning from a game to the shelf. The console exit fix from v2.2.1 remains.
• Diagnostics: clearer cover decoding and local-file errors in /data/PS5GBA/logs/boot.log.

Installation

Download PPSA99209.zip from the release assets, extract the PPSA99209 directory and copy it to /data/homebrew/.…

release.title: XPSemu Alpha 2.1

XPSemu Update 2.1

Up to 4 players
• Every signed-in PS5 user's controller (or a guest's) now works in games. Before, only the first controller was seen.
• Players 2-4 are plugged in within 2 seconds of signing in, even during a game, and unplugged when they sign out.
• Only player 1 controls XPSemu's menus; the other controllers are for the games.

Game language (#10)
• New setting: Settings > Interface > Game language (English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Chinese).
• Games that include that language now start in it. Before, every game started in English.

Saves
• Saves are no longer lost when you leave a game. XPSemu now lets the Xbox finish writing before it stops the game.
• Broken saves are repaired automatically. A save cut off while it was being made could stop a game from saving at all.
• A backup of every change is kept in /data/xemu/save-repair/.
• While the game finishes saving, the Now Playing bar burns away, and you can keep using the menu.

Fixes
• Crash after 15-20 minutes in playing games like Ninja Gaiden Black (#7).
• Crash when a game makes lots of new shaders.
• The Xbox hard disk survives a crash or closing XPSemu from the PS5 home screen. Before, games could hang on loading until xbox_hdd.qcow2 was deleted.
• Far fewer graphics pipelines built, so fewer hitches in effect-heavy scenes.
• No needless ~8 MB cache save every time you leave a game.

Requirements

• kstuff +helper.elf
• ShadowMountPlus
• Your own Xbox MCPX…

apps.name: PS5 Network Mounting
apps.author: sweenyxsky-oss
apps.about:
PS5 Network Mounting is a native PS5 homebrew payload. It connects to an NFS export or an
SMB2/SMB3 share, keeps the connection open, and answers reads for every path under
/hostapp from that share. A small HTTP server on port 18080 serves the control panel.

The payload does not create a kernel mount. It follows the mechanism PS5SX2 uses for its
NFS shares: the protocol client is linked into the payload, the C library's file calls are
redirected with the linker's --wrap, and the payload answers them itself. There is no
/dev/fuse, no libfuse build, and no Itemzflow dependency.

release.title: PS5 Network Mounting v2.1.0
release.notes:
PS5 Network Mounting v2.1.0

The share layer stays in-process: NFS through libnfs and SMB2/SMB3 through
libsmb2 behind one backend, every libc file call under /hostapp answered by
the payload itself. No /dev/fuse, no kernel mount, no Itemzflow.

Fixes

• SMB: the share root is verified by listing it as well as by a stat. Servers
that refuse a CREATE for "/" no longer fail with "is not a readable
folder", and the message now carries the SMB status when libsmb2 has one.
• A short read no longer reports end-of-file; only a zero read or the known
end of the file does.
• Inodes for files whose server sends none are derived from size, time and
mode instead of size alone.
• statvfs on a detaching share reports EIO like every other call.

Changes

• The port is optional. Leave it empty to use the protocol default: SMB 445,
or the NFS portmapper for both the mount and the data connection.
• The panel has a "Use a custom port" tick box, and the reported endpoint
omits a default port.
• Requests served are reported next to open files and bytes served.

Limit

An in-process share is visible to code running inside this payload only.
Other applications on the console cannot see /hostapp.

Included artifact

• PS5NetworkMounting-v2.1.0.elf: PS5 payload built with the organization
SDK, libnfs and libsmb2.

apps.name: PS5 WebKit Autoloader
apps.author: itsPLK
apps.description: An automated payload loader for exploited PS5 consoles
apps.about:
WebKit exploits are usually loaded by pointing your PS5's DNS at some server hosted by someone on the internet. That means you're putting your trust in whoever runs that server — and if it goes down, changes, or disappears, your setup breaks.

There are two ways to set up the autoloader, depending on whether you're already jailbroken.

1. Download webkit-autoloader-installer_vX.Y.Z.elf from the Releases page.

3. The installer opens the browser to cache the autoloader page (choose Poops or Relapse if prompted), creates the WebKit Autoloader app on the homescreen, and exits.
4. Reboot once, then launch WebKit Autoloader from the homescreen.

release.title: NayePlmTools v0.6.3.197
release.notes:
v0.6.3.197 (CN-FORK) — 2026-10-29 · 修「开机不自启」：引导器目录/清单按需创建 + 启动即登记

用户口径：「程序被拉起的时候没有自动创建 autoloader 文件夹，有文件夹也没有写入文件」。

修 bug：/data/ps5_autoloader 不建、清单不写、启动不登记
• 真机取证（192.168.1.214）：目录存在（别的载荷建的），autoload.txt 只有一行 @sync
—— 没有本工具条目、目录里也没有 ELF；本工具那份躺在旧布局
/data/nayeplmtools/payloads/NayePlmTools/NayePlmTools_0.6.3.196-me.elf。
• 四个原因（全在 src/payload_mgr.c）：
1. payload_mgr_bootstrap_self_sync() 第一句 stat(PS5_AUTOLOADER_DIR) 失败就 return
→ 目录不存在时永不创建（.196 那版还专门写了「这个目录归引导器所有，我们不建」）；
2. payload_mgr_autoloader_sync()：目录不存在 return 1；目录在、autoload.txt 不在
时 fopen(...,"r") 失败 → sync skipped + return -1 —— 就是「有文件夹也没写入文件」；
3. 启动对账里「清单没有本工具条目 → leaving it alone」（旧口径「登记只发生在用户明确安装时」）
→ 换机、手清目录、引导器重建清单之后，本工具永远不再自启；
4. 找自己那份 ELF 只扫 payloads/pldmgr 与 local|repo 槽位，**漏了旧布局
payloads//** —— 真机上正好是后者，于是「找不到自己」。
• 改法：
• 新增 autoloader_ensure_dir()：目录不存在 mkdir 0777（容忍 EEXIST），成功/失败都留日志；
• payload_mgr_autoloader_sync() 改用它，autoload.txt 不存在当成空清单继续
（只有 ENOENT 这样，权限等错误仍算失败）；
• payload_mgr_bootstrap_self_sync()：目录/清单按需建；无条目 → 启动即登记
（allow_register=1：落 ELF + 写条目 + 自动补 !1000 延时行，与网页上传同一套）；
新增旧布局扫描；条目在但文件缺失/残包 → 同版本才补，在册版本更新则只留痕、绝不降级。
• 护栏保留：找不到自己那份 ELF → 不写指向空气的条目；候选版本更旧 → 不动。

Fixes the issue where the PS5 freezes when restarting or turning off.

Use at your own risk.

Warning — Automatic mounting/scan with kstuff

Experimental builds with automatic game scanning + mounting

(ShadowMount style) inside kstuff do not yield results.

In real-world tests we will observe:

• kernel panic when disconnecting/reconnecting USB/SSD
• freezing when entering/exiting sleep mode (unmount while in use)
• conflicts with LVD/nullfs mounts and the system sleep cycle

in the same process as kstuff (A53/PPR/BackPork).

Guide

apps.name: Emby5
apps.author: bornaradusin
apps.description: Native Emby client for PlayStation 5
apps.about:
A native Emby and Jellyfin client for a PS5 that runs homebrew. It browses your libraries,
plays films, shows and music with the PS5's own video decoder, and adds Live TV, video on
demand and Seerr requests. The app is PPSA99515, its tile is called Emby5. This is
version 1.3.1.

Emby5 contains no media, channels or subscriptions: it plays what your own server and
providers give you.

1. Download Emby5-.zip from the releases,
unzip it, and copy the PPSA99515/ folder to /data/homebrew/ on the console (or install
it through ProsperoStore).
2. Start Emby5, choose your server from the ones found on your network or enter its
address, and sign in.

release.title: Emby5 1.3.1
release.notes:
What's new

4K playback
• 4K videos, including 4K (UHD) Blu-ray disc images, now get the PS5's hardware video decoder when it couldn't find enough memory before. Emby5 frees the decoders it isn't using for as long as the 4K video plays, and brings them back afterwards.

Installation and updating

1. Close Emby5 completely.
2. Download Emby5-1.3.1.zip from the assets below, not a source-code archive.
3. Extract the ZIP to obtain the PPSA99515/ folder.
4. Copy the complete folder into /data/homebrew/. For an update, merge and overwrite the existing application files.
5. Wait for the transfer to finish, then launch Emby5 and confirm 1.3.1 under Settings > System > Installed version.

apps.name: Afterglow

apps.name: FGG-PlayPods
apps.author: FGGstore
apps.description: Hear your PS5 on any Bluetooth headset — game audio and system sounds streamed over the console's own Bluetooth, no dongle, DualSense stays wireless. Payload for jailbroken PS5.

Game audio and system sounds, through the console's own Bluetooth — no dongle,
and your DualSense stays wireless.

The PS5 has Bluetooth, but no Bluetooth audio. Its radio talks to controllers
and nothing else, and Sony's own wireless headsets need a USB dongle.

FGG-PlayPods changes that. It captures everything the console plays and
streams it to your headset over the PS5's own Bluetooth chip.

release.title: FGG-PlayPods 1.0
release.notes:

apps.name: ps5-solobridge
apps.author: hebiii994
apps.description: PS5 game + system audio on a Focusrite Scarlett Solo (UAC2) over USB - resident payload for jailbroken PS5
apps.about:
Play the PS5's audio (games and system/menu sounds) on a **Focusrite Scarlett Solo
3rd gen** connected to the console's USB port, on a jailbroken PS5.

The PS5 only accepts USB Audio Class 1 devices: the Scarlett Solo is UAC2-only, so the
console ignores it and only offers HDMI output. solobridge is a resident payload that
drives the Solo directly through FreeBSD's /dev/ugen* interface and feeds it the
console mix captured from the system capture service.

Tested on firmware 13.60 with a Scarlett Solo 3rd gen (1235:8211).

Connect the Solo to a PS5 USB port. Sending the payload again while it is running
prints the status of the running instance instead of starting a second one.

release.title: solobridge v0.1.2-test1 (2i2 3rd gen test build)
release.notes:
Test build, not a stable release. Adds the Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 3rd gen (1235:8210) to the devices solobridge looks for. Nothing else changed.

The 2i2 has not been tested on real hardware yet. If you try it, please report back (works or not) with the output of status (echo status | nc 9160), /data/solobridge/log.txt and /data/usbprobe.txt from usbprobe.

• solobridge.elf: stop the old instance first (or reboot), then send it to the ELF loader (port 9021) or put it in /data/pldmgr/payloads/local/solobridge/ for Payload Manager.

Built from the test/2i2-gen3 branch with ps5-payload-sdk.

Visualiser

Stepping through presets follows a shuffled order instead of the alphabet.
Sorted by filename, stepping meant working through one author at a time. The
visualiser also moves on by itself every minute; L2 + Options turns that off.

Keep a track

L2 + Circle writes the playing module into music/ and adds it to
index.txt, so a tune that would otherwise scroll out of the 20 track history
can be kept.

Fixed

The interface named The Mod Archive everywhere, including while downloading
from Modland. Each track now carries where it came from.

Installing

4xx/5xx errors

(H.264, HEVC, AV1, VP9, MPEG-2/4, AAC, AC3, E-AC3, DTS, TrueHD, ALAC,
FLAC, Opus, Vorbis, WMA, PCM) and protocol (HTTP/S, HLS, RTSP, RTP,
UDP, RTMP, MMSH) — compatibility is limited by CPU speed, not codecs

release.title: Wings v.0.1.3
release.notes:
Wings 0.1.3

Wings updates itself

From now on you never copy files to update Wings. When a new version is out, Wings tells you when it starts and opens an update page with four steps:

1. Check - finds the new version.
2. Download - downloads it and checks it against the published SHA-256, with progress and Cancel.
3. Install - puts it in place in a few seconds. Your current version is kept until the new one runs, so nothing is lost if something goes wrong.
4. Restart Wings - close Wings and open it again. That's it.

A small helper inside Wings does the file work (the app itself may not write to /data/homebrew/). It only talks to Wings on the console itself, only downloads this project's official package from GitHub, and quits by itself when done. Details: docs/guides/updating.md.

Downloads

• Dropped downloads reconnect by themselves. At high speeds some debrid hosts cut connections; Wings now restarts the download automatically (up to 3 tries without progress, more as long as data keeps flowing) and shows "Reconnecting in 8 s (try 2 of 3)". Real errors (file removed, disk full) are never retried. Switch: Settings > Pegasus DL > Auto-reconnect dropped downloads.
• Circle cancels any waiting screen at once. "Asking Pegasus DL...", checking a link, Download all parts, loading Pegasus: Circle goes back right away, and a request that answers late changes nothing.
• .pkg links download fast, then install. "PKG to PS5" links now go through Pegasus DL's fast download, then…

release.notes:
HLDRIVE 1.1.3-rc.1 — teste com 48 conexões

Novidades

• Limite de download paralelo triplicado de 16 para 48 conexões por arquivo elegível, mantendo segmentos de 8 MiB e os critérios de validação de intervalos e identidade do arquivo.
• O número efetivo de conexões depende da quantidade de segmentos disponíveis e diminui ao final da transferência. A fila de arquivos permanece sequencial.
• Mantidos os links salvos, idiomas, avisos traduzidos e fundo animado da versão anterior.
• Corrigido o registro incorreto de velocidade acima de 500 Mbps: o usuário esclareceu que essa velocidade nunca foi alcançada.

Instalação

Baixe HLDRIVE.1.1.3-rc.1.elf e seu HLDRIVE.1.1.3-rc.1.elf.sha256. Encerre o payload anterior e inicie o novo ELF pelo loader. Renomeie para HLDRIVE.elf se o seu método exigir esse nome.

Recarregue http://IP_DO_PS5:8081. A interface deve indicar 1.1.3-rc.1; em arquivos elegíveis, o painel deve mostrar até 48.

Validação e limitações

Os 21 cenários HTTPS locais passaram com verificação dos dados baixados, incluindo transferências de 400 MiB + 123 bytes usando 48 conexões, fallback sequencial, cancelamento e rejeição de respostas inválidas. Esses testes usam um servidor sintético e não medem a velocidade do Google Drive ou do PS5.

Build do frontend, checagem de traduções e compilação do ELF concluídos. A suíte offline completa não foi executada nesta alteração; há falha preexistente documentada envolvendo RemoveSettingsAt.

O aumento é experimental: não garante…

apps.about:
Chūkei DNS is a lightweight DNS relay server. It provides DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) functionality to bypass DNS hijacking by ISPs and other network intermediaries while offering domain filtering capabilities to block unwanted connections like system updates and telemetry.

Primary Use Case
On PlayStation®4/PlayStation®5 systems, Chūkei DNS integrates as a plugin within HEN payloads. By setting the console's DNS to 127.0.0.1, the system cannot resolve domain names until a payload containing Chūkei DNS is executed. Once active, DNS resolution is restored with filtering and DoH protection enabled.

apps.name: FGG Unpack
apps.author: FGGstore
apps.description: Extract .zip and .7z archives directly on a jailbroken PlayStation 5. Drop an archive in a watched folder and it unpacks in place — upload 30 GB instead of 150.
apps.about:
Extract .zip and .7z archives directly on a jailbroken PlayStation 5.

A jailbroken PS5 has no way to unpack an archive. Anything that arrives
compressed — homebrew bundles, asset packs, emulator data, disk images — has to
be extracted on a PC first and then copied over FTP file by file.

That is slow, and it is slow in the worst possible way: you end up transferring
the uncompressed size.

FGG Unpack runs in the background on the console, watches a folder, and unpacks
whatever you drop into it.

Measured on real hardware: a 31 GB archive containing a 152 GB image.
Uploading it took ~40 minutes. Uploading the extracted image would have taken
over three hours at the same link speed.

A lightweight, standalone PS5 payload that restores the console's system date
and time using public NTP servers.

It is intended for consoles with a depleted, disconnected, or faulty CMOS/RTC
battery where the clock resets after the PS5 is completely powered off.

Download the latest precompiled ps5-date-time-sync.elf from the
Releases
page.

1. Connect the PS5 to the Internet.
2. Inject or launch ps5-date-time-sync.elf with a compatible payload loader.
3. Wait for the notification.
4. The payload attempts to synchronize the clock and then exits automatically.

release.title: PS5 Time & Date Sync v1.0.0
release.notes:
PS5 Time & Date Sync by Deckerr97

Initial public release.

A standalone, one-shot PS5 payload that restores the console date and time using public NTP servers. It is designed for consoles whose CMOS/RTC battery no longer retains the clock after a complete shutdown.

Features

• Automatic NTP date and time synchronization
• Published Cloudflare numeric fallbacks when PS5 DNS is unavailable
• Cloudflare, pool.ntp.org, and Google Public NTP hostname fallbacks
• NTP endpoint, version, mode, stratum, request timestamp, and date validation
• Clock read-back verification after updating
• Preserves the configured PS5 timezone
• One notification per payload execution
• No application installation or file modification
• Automatically exits after completion

Requirements

• Compatible PS5 exploit and ELF payload loader
• Internet access with outbound UDP port 123
• An execution environment that permits settimeofday

Built using a PS5 Payload SDK package containing firmware definitions through 13.60. Actual runtime compatibility depends on the firmware, exploit, loader, and available permissions.

Acknowledgements

Special thanks to John Törnblom and every contributor to the PS5 Payload SDK for creating and maintaining the toolchain that made this payload possible.

Build verification

• File: ps5-date-time-sync.elf
• Size: 130,240 bytes
• SHA-256: 91806229803845930B2173174E1AFEADF509E4C171F6396788F929558FAD6849

apps.name: ps5-fan-control
apps.author: owendswang
apps.description: Small PS5 daemon keeps applying fan temperature threshold.
apps.about:
Small PS5 daemon payload ELF that sets the system fan temperature threshold through /dev/icc_fan.

It does not implement its own fan curve. The PS5 system fan driver still handles automatic fan speed changes; this payload only changes and re-applies the temperature threshold used by that driver.

The payload sets its process name to ps5-fan-control.elf. Launching it again kills the previous ps5-fan-control.elf process, then continues running as a restarted daemon.

apps.description: Standalone PS5 on-console payload to move apps between Games/Media tabs and hide offline PSN bloatware (Universal FW 5.00 – 13.60)
apps.about:
A lightweight on-console utility and web interface for jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles (FW 5.00 through 13.60) that gives you complete control over your PS5 Home Screen layout.

On modern PS5 firmwares, Sony splits dashboard data across two synchronized databases:

Modifying only one database causes the system shell to restore stale metadata from cache, corrupt concept bitmasks (causing game padlocks), or revert changes after entering Rest Mode.

TabShifter updates all database layers simultaneously, applies the correct concept bitmasks (1162 / 2236), and safely reloads SceShellUI in ~1.5 seconds without causing database rebuild prompts.

release.title: PS5 TabShifter v1.3.0
release.notes:
What’s New in v1.3.0

Universal Firmware Engine (FW 5.00 – 13.60): Sony changed how dashboard JSON is stored between earlier firmwares and 11.40+. TabShifter now dynamically handles both legacy field_list arrays (FW 5.00–10.xx) and modern flat JSON (FW 11.00–13.60) across both app.db and appinfo.db.

Permanent Rest Mode Bloatware Suppression: Previously, hiding apps like PlayStation Store or PS Plus would revert after waking the console or cold booting. v1.3.0 sets native daemon flags (pushed: false), clears emsPushedFlag, and purges system group entries so hidden bloatware stays gone.

Padlock Bug Resolved + One-Click "Fix Padlocks" Tool: Padlocks happen when concept metadata is modified with standard app display IDs instead of Sony's native concept bitmasks (1162 for Games, 2236 for Media). v1.3.0 enforces proper bitmasks across all tables and includes an orange "Fix Padlocks" button in the dashboard to instantly restore entitlements across your entire library if another tool locked your games.

Multi-User Profile Sync: TabShifter now scans all profile tables (tbl_iconinfo_* / tbl_concepticoninfo_*), ensuring your customized layout and hidden tiles stay identical across every account on the console.

Web UI Quality-of-Life Upgrades:

1. No Viewport Jumping: Editing, pinning, or hiding titles near the bottom no longer scrolls the page back to the top.

2. Live Search & Filter Pills: Quickly filter your dashboard by All, Games, Media, Hidden, PS5, PS4, or Homebrew.

apps.name: PS5CLEAN
apps.author: Yahballon
apps.description: This tool helps you
apps.about:
PS5CLEAN is a native PS5 homebrew fun app with a sci-fi dashboard and timed fan pulses. The idea is simple: let the fan alternate between high and low cooling, in the hope that the changing airflow might loosen a little dust inside the console.

That is the hope, not a proven cleaning effect. PS5CLEAN is an experimental project, not a replacement for physical cleaning or maintenance.

Rendered from the actual app UI. This preview is not connected to a console, so live readings are blank.

Press Start Cleaning to begin. The first half of each pulse interval requests high cooling using a 20 C temperature target. The second half requests low cooling using a 60 C target. The cycle repeats until the selected duration ends or you press Stop.

apps.description: Turns off the PlayStation 5's continuous recent-gameplay recording. With nothing encoded, there is nothing for the console to save.
apps.about:
Hush is a small payload for jailbroken consoles that turns off the console's
continuous "recent gameplay" recording. With nothing encoded, there is nothing
for the console to save.

Every PS5 encodes the last 15 seconds to one hour of gameplay all the time.
Sony exposes the clip length, never an off switch. The data lands in a reserved
area of the internal NVMe, so it does not show up in any storage screen.

On a 13.60 console a saved 15-second clip is ~31.6 MB. Read as the buffer's
bitrate, that is roughly 7–8 GB written per hour of play — an inference from
the clip size; no readable storage counter was found.

release.title: Hush 1.1.1
release.notes:
A leftover state.txt no longer looks like a live patch

/data/hush/state.txt exists while the patch is in place and is deleted once
every slot is restored. Tools read it that way: PS5Upload's upcoming hold-mode
support (phantomptr/ps5upload#651)
waits for the file to go before starting a stream.

A reboot drops the patch but not the file. After a boot with hold_s=0, a
console switched to hold mode kept the old state.txt until the first game's
window ended. Until then every stream would wait and pause for nothing.

In hold mode Hush now checks on start, and on enabled=0, whether any slot is
redirected. If none is, it deletes the leftover file and logs:

Checked on 13.60 with a planted state.txt from an earlier boot: removed at start.

Nothing else changed. With hold_s=0 the next start patches again and rewrites
the file, as before.

Install

Replace hush.elf in Payload Manager. Existing config.ini files keep working.

Build

Reproducible with the same toolchain (-Wl,--build-id=none): two clean builds of
this tag gave this exact binary. Built with Homebrew clang/LLD 23.1.4.

apps.about:
该 payload 把整套前端（HTML/CSS/JS/图形）内嵌进 ELF 并压缩，因此部署只是一个文件，无需额外安装任何东西。

版本在哪里显示。 启动器（以及 etaHEN 的 plugins / payload ELFs 菜单）按文件名列出 payload，所以版本号刻意放在文件名里：构建产物为 PS5-Mango-v1.1.elf。在 Makefile 里改动 VERSION_TAG 会重命名产物——这也是主机上唯一能显示的版本标识。payload 还会在启动通知、stdout 以及 /api/status 接口中上报版本。

解压覆盖 .zip、.zipx、.7z、.rar、.001、.tar、.gz、.bz2、.xz、.zst、.lzh、.cab、.cpio、.arj、.pmd、.xar 以及常见的双后缀（.tar.gz、.tbz2、.txz …），包括加密归档与分卷。

解压在进程内完成：payload 自带由 UnRAR（RAR）、LZMA SDK（7z）以及 minizip-ng + zlib（zip/zipx）构建的引擎——无需外部 helper ELF。加密归档（zip/7z/RAR 的 ZipCrypto、AES）直接支持：当归档需要密码时，UI 会向你索取并传给引擎。进度按条目上报，中断的解压可在 payload 重启后续传。分卷可从任意分卷入队——引擎会将其归一化为首卷。

release.title: PS5-Mango v1.1
release.notes:
PS5 Mango v1.1 发布说明

一、新增

1. NAS 支持 WebDAV / WebDAVS（HTTPS）

现在 PS5 可以直接当 WebDAV 客户端连群晖、飞牛、TrueNAS、Alist、Windows IIS 这类服务端。

2. 页内播放器

现在视频和音频直接在页面里播。

• 进度条可以拖动，不必从头重放。
• 播放不再创建下载任务，右下角任务坞不会因为看个片子亮起来。
• 视频与音频共用同一个面板：音频没有画面，面板里显示一枚音频图标 + 底部自绘控制条。

3. NAS 书签条不再溢出

v1.0 的书签区是一个 inline-flex 单体：8 个书签会拼成 2400 px 的一个整体，容器只有约 1070 px，
第 5 个之后滚不到也点不到，+ NAS 被挤到第三行，单条长地址能撑到 414 px 并折成两行。

• 书签区改为可折行、单条限宽（240px × --ui，约 300 px），+ NAS 移进书签流内部。
• 长地址按像素预算缩短，末端目录名永远保留（davs:…/自动备份），完整地址留在 title 里。
• 两行封顶，放不下的收进「更多 N」，点开就地展开成「收起」。
• 1～4 个书签与 v1.0 完全一致，日常用户看不出区别。

4. 存档：删完之后不再留空壳

删掉某游戏的最后一份存档后，空的 sdimg_ 目录与 _meta/ 目录现在会自动收尾，
浏览页也会跳过 slots == 0 的空条目——不再出现「这个游戏一份存档都没有，卡片却还在」的幽灵卡片。

5. 上传/导入进度面板可以关掉了

上传进度是浏览器端的合成行（服务端并没有对应任务），v1.0 里它在上传结束后可能残留 100%，
点 下一帧又被弹回来。现在：清理责任移进上传函数本身（try/finally）、点 直接丢弃、
60 秒心跳过期兜底、合成行不再显示「取消」按钮（点了只会拿到 404）。

二、优化

• 粘贴/复制文件不再变成空文件夹：列目录前先用 PROPFIND Depth:0 探 resourcetype，
确认是集合才建目录；文件直接写。此前把文件误判为目录，落地成一个空文件夹。
• 报错信息带实际请求路径：webdav: not found 这类消息现在能看出是哪条 URL 失败。
• 文件名上限 256 → 512 字节，长中文名不再被截断。
• 存档列表：前端显式判断 slots != null，不再把「0 个槽位」和「字段缺失」混为一谈。

English summary

Added — WebDAV / WebDAVS (HTTPS) shares on top of the existing SMB/NFS backends, with
in-place HTTP ⇄ HTTPS switching for existing bookmarks and SNI on handshake; an in-page
video/audio player backed by GET /api/fs/raw with HTTP Range (206/416, seekable, no
download task); a rebuilt NAS bookmark bar that wraps, caps each chip, shortens long
addresses by pixel budget (last path segment always visible) and folds…

apps.name: ps5-signal
apps.author: Marice
apps.description: PS5 background payload that plays beep tunes and LED colour patterns for homebrew, through a small HTTP API on 127.0.0.1
apps.about:
A background payload for the PS5 that plays beep sequences and LED sequences (brightness and colour)
for other homebrew. It runs once, listens on 127.0.0.1:9150 and takes simple HTTP requests with a JSON body,
so a payload, a game port or a web page on the console can beep or light the console without calling its
internal functions itself. A homebrew app can't drive these itself: they need a system process's rights, which
only this payload takes.

There is no free RGB colour: the LED has blue, white and amber light only. The LED state holds a record per channel;
each channel is a small program of steps (the system's own light fades this way). A colour is set by rewriting each
channel as a single step that holds its level. Whether the LED has zones that can be lit separately is not known yet.
Firmware 9.00 or newer.

release.title: ps5-smbd 0.3.0
release.notes:
New

• SMB 3.1.1, next to 3.0 and 3.0.2. Windows 11 now connects with 3.1.1, and a PC that requires 3.1.1 can connect at all.
• libsmb2 master. The fixes reported in sahlberg/libsmb2#500 are now upstream, so ps5-smbd builds against libsmb2's public API, with one patch left of seven. This also brings in:
• The negotiate check is always signed. When a PC does not require signing (RequireSecuritySignature off), 0.2.0 and older answered this check unsigned, and Windows refuses that.
• A second session no longer drops the first. A second Windows logon session on the same connection, such as an administrator prompt next to Explorer, now takes over the connection, and Explorer logs in again by itself.
• Listings answer four more information classes.
• No data races when signing from several threads.
• README: "If Windows cannot connect". This new section covers:
• what ps5-smbd speaks and what it does not;
• the PC settings to check;
• remembered credentials;
• how to make a trace;
• what the net use errors mean.

Thanks to libsmb2's maintainer, who merged the fixes and opened the pull request that moved ps5-smbd to libsmb2 master.

Glint only works in 60 Hz mode. If a game switches the PS5 to 120 Hz, capture stops until you restart the console.

Lower latency

• Sound recovers after a console freeze: it skips the backlog instead of playing up to a second behind for half a minute.

The payload now streams at 35 Mbit/s (was 50). Over Wi-Fi, busy games at 50 Mbit/s or more could stall for a second or two; 35 stays at a steady 60 fps. With the PS5 on a cable you can go higher with the bitrate=N start argument (up to 100 Mbit/s) for a sharper picture in busy scenes.

release.title: Stella PS5 1.0.2

Stella PS5 1.0.2

Fixes from an audit of the whole port. Nothing changes in how the app looks or plays.

Fixed

• Out of memory. A failed memory allocation now raises C++'s std::bad_alloc, and the code that can handle it catches it. Stella's state loading is one such place: a damaged state file that asked for gigabytes stopped the app; now that state just doesn't load. With Settings > SYSTEM > Debug logs on, the start-up check in boot.log (exceptions: ok) covers it too.
• Version number in the build. A new version number now rebuilds everything that carries it. Before, an update could still say the old version was running.
• Updates (the helper's HTTPS client).
• A malformed chunked answer from the server is refused at once, instead of being read past its size limit.
• A redirect from HTTPS down to plain HTTP isn't followed.
• Update journal. It now checks each file's whole SHA-256 instead of its first MiB, so a big eboot.bin put back after an interrupted update is recognised correctly.
• Shelf. It no longer waits for ever if the system refuses its drawing threads.
• Crash report. The report in boot.log is now written whole even when the faulting code keeps no frame pointer.

Updating

• From 1.0.1: Settings > SYSTEM > Updates offers 1.0.2. Or send StellaPS5-v1.0.2.elf to your payload loader (port 9021).

apps.description: Read-only PS5 process and decrypted module (SPRX/SELF) dumper with VA<->offset index.
apps.about:
PS5 payload that extracts the decrypted in-memory image of a loaded SPRX/SELF module from a
live process, with a VA↔offset index that Ghidra and IDA can load directly.

On the console a module exists twice. The .sprx on disk is encrypted and signed; the copy in
memory is the decrypted, relocated image the CPU actually runs. Analysing the file needs keys and
a SELF parser. Analysing the live image needs neither — it is plain x86-64 with its imports
already resolved.

sprxdump takes the second road: it asks the kernel where the module is mapped and copies it out.

You run one file on the console. It sets the system up, the console goes to rest mode, and it wakes into Linux.

Your PS5's firmware isn't modified and nothing is flashed — a reboot puts everything back the way it was. While it runs, the loader does patch the running system in memory: that's how it prepares the handoff, and it's gone on the next boot.

The files it writes are diagnostic: a log, written to the USB drive and to /data on the console so it survives a crash.

Updating Linux on a PS5 isn't the usual path. release.notes:
Linux Loader AIO

Boot Linux on a PS5 (Phat or Slim) that's on firmware 12.xx. One file.

What this is

Our own build, from our own 12.xx offset tables, with extra sanity checks. It writes ps5lin_probe.log to the USB drive's boot partition — adding to it each run, so the whole history is kept — which is what a failure gets diagnosed from instead of guessed at.

It's built for 12.xx. Anything outside 12.xx is refused by design.

If you're on a different firmware, upstream's ps5-linux project builds a loader that covers more: https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-loader

Their last proper release is v2.5 from 5 September 2026 — anything they've merged since exists only in their repository, so you'd be building it yourself.

The file

ps5-linux-loader-12xx-ONLY-aio.elf

• Firmware: 12.00 · 12.02 · 12.20 · 12.40 · 12.60 · 12.70
• Console: PS5 (Phat) or PS5 Slim

Or build it yourself

The source is public: https://github.com/Wigglez-sudo/12.xx-linux-loader-dev-base

You need the PS5 payload SDK — https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk — following its own README. It expects to live at /opt/ps5-payload-sdk; set PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK if you put it elsewhere.

Before you start

• Use an SSD in a USB enclosure if you can. It boots far quicker and avoids the loader not finding the image in time, which is the most common failure.

apps.name: youtube-update-blocker
apps.author: Forte500
apps.description: PS5 payload that blocks YouTube updates by patching appinfo.db in place, universal: US/EU/JP.
apps.about:
A single ELF payload that patches the console's app database in place —
no SQLite engine, no intermediate app, no structural changes.

On the PS5, /system_data/priv/mms/appinfo.db is a SQLite database that
holds the metadata of every installed app. For YouTube it stores the
installed version and the URL the system queries for version information.

The console then believes YouTube is already at an unreachable version and
has no server to query for updates.

The payload is deliberately minimal: it does not embed a SQLite
engine. It walks the database b-tree, locates the live cells, and
overwrites only the bytes of the two values — keeping their length
identical, so no header, varint, cell or page ever changes.

release.title: v1.0 — PS5 Pro 12.xx loader
release.notes:
Boot Linux on a PS5 Pro on firmware 12.xx.

Files

The single-firmware builds are the same code as the AIO, restricted to one firmware — use one if you want to rule out the AIO choosing the wrong table. Every build checks the console and refuses anything that isn't a Pro.

Firmware

What it does on a Pro

• Reads the hypervisor at 0x8E0000000 instead of the base carveout.
• Dumps the console's GPU firmware — eight viola_*.bin files — to lib/firmware/amdgpu/ on the USB boot partition. Images built for the Pro pick them up at boot; on Bazzite Deck the first boot installs them, and starting Linux with the loader once more is what makes them take.
• Writes loader-1240-trace.txt and ps5lin_probe.log to the boot partition, appending each run, so a failure can be read rather than guessed at.

Firmware isn't modified and nothing is flashed — a reboot puts everything back. The loader does patch the running system in memory while it runs.

Before you start

• An SSD in a USB enclosure, with the image on its boot partition. A stick often works but is the usual reason the loader can't find the image in time.
• Your console already jailbroken, and a way to send the ELF to it.

If it doesn't boot

Power off, move the drive to a different USB port, run it again. Then send loader-1240-trace.txt — it says which stage it reached.

Source

Build it yourself from pro-aio/ in this repository: https://github.com/Wigglez-sudo/12.xx-linux-loader-pro-beta

release.title: DevilutionX for PS5 1.0.0
release.notes:
A native PS5 build of DevilutionX, as an installed title (PPSA98514). It is a separate port from the payload one in Packaging/ps5 and does not replace it. The sources are in ps5port/.

What is better than the payload port in Packaging/ps5

• Launches from the home screen. It installs as a title with its own icon, background pictures and start-up sound. The payload port has to be started from a browser (ps5-payload-websrv) or its companion launcher.
• Vulkan output at 3840x2160. The picture goes to the TV through Vulkan (RADV on VK_KHR_display), about 60 Hz. Each frame goes up through a staging buffer and a GPU copy.
• 720p by default. The game draws at 1280x720 instead of the 640x480 the core defaults to, and the GPU scales it.
• Settings that fit a console. Fullscreen, Fit to Screen and Frame Rate Control are hidden (the PS5 is always full screen and synchronised to the TV), and Nearest Pixel is the default scaling quality.
• Follows the console's language. On the first start the game uses the language set in the PS5's system settings (Spanish from Spain and from Latin America both give Spanish). A language chosen in the game's settings still wins afterwards.
• Your files stay out of the app folder. Game files, saves and diablo.ini live in /data/DevilutionX/, so installing or updating the app never touches them.
• Opens /data by itself. It asks LegacyJB, etaHEN or OnionHEN for access at start-up and falls back to the Lapy helper.
• One command to build, package and deploy.…

A homebrew build of LostOdysseyRecomp for PlayStation 5 consoles that run homebrew titles. Now in beta.

Download · Install guide · Upstream project · License: GPL-3.0

LostOdysseyRecomp turns the Xbox 360 game into native code by static recompilation. This fork adds a PS5 target: the game runs as a homebrew title (PPSA99212) on the console's own CPU and GPU, rendering through Vulkan with Mesa's RADV driver built for the PS5.

You need your own copy of the game. This repository contains no game data, no shaders taken from the game and no Sony code.

release.title: Lost Odyssey PS5 – Beta (build 50)
release.notes:
Beta (build 50)

Faster startup
• The game now starts in about 3 seconds instead of about 22. At every start the game was reading through its whole 1.8 GB built-in shader cache, one entry at a time, before showing anything. It now keeps a small index next to that cache (cache/shaders/builtin_v28_spirv.lostore.index) and reads that instead.
• The first start after updating still takes the old time while the index is built. Every start after that is fast. If the shader cache changes, the index is rebuilt automatically.

Also in this build (from build 48)
• No more "eboot.bin error" when the game can't find your discs: a notification now says where the files go. (#1)
• "Prepare shaders again" removed from Settings → System; it did nothing on the PS5.

Updating
Replace eboot.bin in /data/homebrew/PPSA99212/. Shaders, discs, saves and ps5-env.txt stay as they are.

eboot.bin SHA-256: b5683aff3bf889d3c17bfb8f1143c0a674794681030d000c3b4ff037860f3ceb

PS5SD 1.0.0 is the version that keeps its promises: every item of the 1.0 checklist in ROADMAP.md holds. From here on, a change that breaks a client of the API needs a new major version.

What 1.0 means

• The API is fixed: one error shape with a code, progress as server-sent events, POST /sdapi/v1/options waits for the model, the model of an OpenAI request switches it, and an OpenAPI description at /ps5sd/v1/app/openapi.json (0.9.15 to 0.9.17).
• No run fails without a reason: the web UI says before a run when it may not fit and what to lower; a run that fails anyway says why (0.9.18).
• No known crash: the two ends 0.9.18's measurements found are fixed, and there is no open bug.

An update keeps everything

• Tested on the console from every release since 0.5.0 (26 releases): install the old one, make models, LoRAs, presets, images, settings and an API key through its API, update to 1.0, and check that all of it is still there. All 26 passed. scripts/update-test.py does it again for any build.

A soak test

• 38 minutes of mixed load on the console: 22 model switches between Z-Image Turbo, SDXL, FLUX.2 Klein 9B with a LoRA and Wan 2.1, 36 jobs with three queued at once, a cancel while a job runs, a video, and an event stream open all along. Every job and switch did what it should, each round took the same time, and the CPU heap stayed at 0.63 to 0.66 GiB after the first round. scripts/soak-test.py runs it again. The numbers are in CONSOLE.md.
